title: Generosity part 2
devotional:
2 Corinthians 8:1-9

‘’And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the Macedonian churches. In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity. For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own, they urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the Lord’s people. And they exceeded our expectations: They gave themselves first of all to the Lord, and then by the will of God also to us. So we urged Titus, just as he had earlier made a beginning, to bring also to completion this act of grace on your part. But since you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness and in the love we have kindled in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving. I am not commanding you, but I want to test the sincerity of your love by comparing it with the earnestness of others. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.’’

Generosity is a familiar concept; hopefully there have been times in all our lives when others have come to us and shown us great kindness. Or there have been times when we have had the opportunity to be generous to others. However, our understanding of generosity is usually defined by two things, ‘giving’ or ‘receiving’. Although ‘giving’ and ‘receiving’ are integral parts of generosity, we need to understand that as far as the bible is concerned generosity is so much more than this. You could even say that the giving and receiving components of generosity are more the consequences or the fruit of generosity.

Generosity is first and foremost a deep rooted characteristic that should be the distinguishing feature of people who are known as Christians. Generosity is the essence of community. A group of people cannot become a community of God if generosity is not a tangible growing reality.

So we want to explore an example of generosity from the bible and try and grasp what it really is.

2 Corinthians 8-9 is probably the best exposition of generosity you are ever going to come across.

Before we look at these verses I need to say a few things: -

Paul is using the Macedonian churches (Philippi and Thessalonica) as an example to encourage the church in Corinth to continue to collect money for the poor in Jerusalem. The Christians in Jerusalem had suffered greatly. They were ostracized by their communities which meant that they lost all opportunity to sell their goods or trade; they were also prohibited from buying everyday things like food, clothing, and other essentials. Their problem was made worse by a severe famine that had devastated the whole area of Judea.

Paul was not using the example of the Macedonian churches to make the Christians in Corinth feel guilty or ashamed. Rather he wanted them to see how the power of grace leads to authentic generosity. The Christians in Macedonia lived in extreme poverty, but they gave, and gave.

When the translators translated 2 Corinthians 8-9 they used the word generous to translate two very different Greek words. The first word is Haplotēs which means arising out of purity of mind. In other words, this ‘giving’ to those in need arose from pure intentions. See 2 Cor 8:1, 9:11 9:13. It could be understood as focused.

However, I don’t think God wants our generosity to be expressed in the same way we pay tax. There needs to be intentionality about generosity.

The second word eulogia means to bless, to praise or celebrate. These two words are two sides of the same ‘coin.’ The first word describes the character of the generous person, while the second word describes the effect on others a generous person has.

Remember the point of this passage is to encourage the Church in Corinth to care for the poor Christians in Jerusalem. It seems that in his word God encourages voluntary giving for his work, but compulsory giving to the poor. In the New Testament Christians are encouraged to give to the poor see Matthew 5:42 Acts 20:35, Romans 12:13, Galatians 2:9-10, Ephesians 4:28, Hebrews 13:16, James 1:27. They are also told that they should provide for those who teach Galatians 6:6, 1Timothy 5:17-18 1Corinthians 9:1-14. If you read this passage carefully it is interesting what is not said. Using the Church of Macedonia as an example of generosity, Paul says nothing what so ever about how much they gave, it seems that the amount they gave was irrelevant.
prayer: Father may generosity be an indicator that you are changing my heart.
